title: Orchestrator handbook for staggered canaries (working notes)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working handbook for the release orchestrator role and cross-functional runbook for staggered canaries. Focus is on multi-dimension canaries (region, model-variant, pricing-tier) that require coordinated human/automation choreography. Intention: document pragmatic steps, heuristics, and a small set of standardized probes that teams can reuse.

Audience:
- Release orchestrators (primary)
- Product managers and Eng leads coordinating exposure
- SRE/oncall engineers implementing gates and metrics
- Growth/Analytics owners for experiment measurement

High-level goals:
1) Reduce human friction when coordinating multi-wave exposures.
2) Provide clear, observable decision points with explicit owners.
3) Make rollbacks predictable and reversible by automating escape hatches.
4) Keep cost & latency budgets visible and part of gating logic.

Core concepts and definitions (quick):
- Staggered canary: progressive activation across orthogonal slices (geo, model, cohort). Not a single traffic ramp — may advance one axis at a time.
- Orchestrator: person (or automation) who runs the exposure script, marks gates as pass/fail, triggers synthetic sweeps.
- Steward: team-level on-call representative who owns product-level judgment and downstream comms.
- Safety probe: an automated check (latency, error rate, semantic-sanity) that must pass for a slice to proceed.

Recipe: pre-launch checklist (day -3 to day 0)
- Readout & hypothesis: 1-paragraph expected impact and failure modes (owner: PM).
- Risk slices enumerated: list explicit cohorts that might be sensitive (e.g., auth flows, billing flows, heavy-rerank users). (owner: PM + SE).
- Capacity check: verify reserved pool, headroom, and fallback region capacity (owner: infra).
- Observability wiring: dashboards provisioned, alert thresholds set, debug traces enabled for model pipeline. (owner: observability).
- Synthetic suite: short canonical prompts + edge prompts + privacy-sensitive prompts created and added to smoke harness. (owner: QA/ME).
- Comms plan: stakeholder cadence, escalation recipients, and pre-written rollback comms. (owner: release comms).

On the day (orchestrator playbook)
1) Dry-run in staging: run the synthetic harness end-to-end and capture golden metrics. If divergence > tolerated delta, do not proceed.
2) Activate slice 0 (1% regional traffic or 1% cohort). Start 15 minute observation window.
3) Automated probes (run every 60s): P50/P95 latency change, request error rate, model-quality spike (semantic regression score), cost-per-token delta.
4) Orchestrator triage window (15 min): If any probe trips a critical threshold, mark FAIL -> immediate rollback of slice and notify steward. If all probes green, advance to intra-day ramp (to 5%).
5) For multi-axis exposures: advance only one axis at a time (e.g., expand model-variant within same region before expanding region).

Signal catalog (recommended probes and thresholds)
- Latency P95 (end-to-end): delta > +40% or P95 > 1200ms => red.
- Request error rate: > 0.5% increase absolute or > 3x baseline (whichever larger) => red.
- Semantic regression probe (synthetic prompts): fraction of failing cases > 2% relative => amber if 2-5%, red >5%.
- Cost per 1k tokens: unexpected delta > +30% => amber; automation will check budget reserve.
- Sticky-identities: user session dropout or increased re-auths > 1% => red.
- Human-reported escalations: any curated complaint from steward or CS about hallucination/incorrectness => immediate amber and possible red if reproducible.

Decision matrix (quick)
- Green: all critical probes green for 30m => proceed to next ramp.
- Amber: non-critical probes triggered (third-party latency, small semantic blips). Orchestrator consults Steward and Metrics owner; may hold or rollback to previous slice.
- Red: critical probe triggered or large user impact. Immediate rollback, postmortem trigger.

Rollback and escape hatches
- Automated rollback: route-switcher job that returns traffic to baseline model/region within 30s. Orchestrator triggers via CLI: redwood rollout revert --exposure-id <id> --to-baseline.
- Soft-fallback: switch to cheaper/older model variant in that slice if available (useful for cost/latency regressions).
- Circuit breaker: global kill-switch if cross-slice correlation patterns indicate systemic failure.

Stakeholder choreography and comms
- Pre-activation 10m ping: orchestrator posts to #release-ops with expected timeline.
- Post-activation 5m summary: automated snapshot posted to #release-ops and stakeholder email thread.
- Escalation ladder: steward -> SRE lead -> Eng PM -> Eng Director -> Exec incident liaison.
- Post-rollback comms: templated message with impact summary, action taken, next steps, and link to postmortem doc.

Observability templates (minimum dashboards)
- Slice-indexed latency and error rate time-series with baseline overlay.
- Synthetic probe feed with per-prompt pass/fail and highlighted diffs.
- Model token-utilization and cost telemetry by slice variant.
- User-impact feed: DAU exposure, cancellation events, billing anomalies.

Micro-cohort stitching rules (when to merge slices)
- If two slices show indistinguishable signal for 24h and no edge-case regressions, they can be merged and treated as a single traffic allocation.
- If merging increases exposure to a sensitive cohort, require an explicit steward sign-off.

Automated tooling snippets (examples)
- Start exposure: redwood rollout start --name "news-rerank-canary" --slice-config slices.yaml --dry-run=false
- Snapshot metrics: redwood observability snapshot --slice id=canary-001 --since 15m --metrics latency,error,semantic
- Revert: redwood rollout revert --exposure-id canary-001 --reason "semantic regression"

Synthetic traffic recipe (short)
- 60% normal prompts drawn from production-type corpus (small sample)
- 20% edge-case prompts (truncation, long context, ambiguous asks)
- 10% adversarial sanity-checks (prompts known to trip hallucinations)
- 10% privacy/security-sensitive prompts (should score pass on safety checks)

Postmortem & learning loop
- Trigger threshold: any red rollback must spawn a postmortem doc within 48h.
- Minimum sections: timeline, metrics, root cause hypothesis, remediation plan, roll-forward plan, owners.
- Store canonical remediation templates in Confluence and link back to rollout ticket.

Open questions and TODOs (working list)
- How to quantify semantic regression across multilingual prompts? Need small translation-validation harness. (owner: applied-ml)
- Automating cost-aware gating: should cost delta be a hard gate or an advisory amber? Need stakeholder alignment. (owner: finance/product)
- Formalizing the merge-window rules for micro-cohorts longer than 48h.

Appendix: quick checklists (one-liners)
- Pre-flight: dashboards + synthetic suite + capacity = go/no-go.
- First slice: watch automated probes for 15m.
- Ramp step: only one axis per ramp.
- If a critical probe trips: revert, notify, and document.

Notes to self (informal):
- Prototype a small 'orchestrator CLI' that wires the snapshot and revert commands into a single button. Explore linking with console rollouts UI for live buttons.
- Consider adding a lightweight 'stability score' combining p95 latency, error-rate, and semantic probe into a single index for quick human judgment.

If you're reading this and have war stories or suggestions, add to the comments or ping me (Sofia). Will iterate into a more formal playbook after two runs.

Related tickets/refs: RUN-4123 (canary orchestrator P0), PR#889 (console rollout quick actions), Confluence: Canary Orchestration Spec.

---- end of doc ----
